supporting_observations.claim: At 13:39:57, WS-MLOPEZ-01 recorded a network logon for omar.haddad from WS-OHADDAD-01; the PowerShell process shortly afterward used the same Omar logon ID.

At 13:41:49, PowerShell ran the command shown as the organization's known workstation patching method: executing \\FILE-HD-01\IT\Deploy-Patches.ps1. The inventory says Omar performs patching this way and workstation patching was scheduled during business hours.

PowerShell launched wusa.exe to install a Windows update package quietly, and the proxy recorded a Windows Update Agent connection downloading about 38.8 MB. This is consistent with the patching activity, though it does not independently verify the script's contents.
The PowerShell process ended at 13:42:39. Its timing is near the reported brief window, although the available records do not directly establish whether a window was visible to Maria.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied coverage status reports winsec, Sysmon, proxy, Zeek connection, and DNS collection as available for WS-MLOPEZ-01 during the review window; the listed collection outage is on WS-LPARK-01, not the alerted host.
The records show the PowerShell command line and its child process, but do not provide the contents, hash, or signature of Deploy-Patches.ps1 or the installed update package.
claims_not_established: Whether Maria saw a visible PowerShell window; process creation records alone do not establish window visibility.
Whether Deploy-Patches.ps1 or the update package contents were authentic and unmodified.
Whether the user-reported timing refers to the PowerShell launch at 13:41:49 or another event.
unrelated_findings: Separate review: Kerberos activity from WS-MLOPEZ-01 requested a ticket for ben.carter and was followed by a network logon for ben.carter on WS-BCARTER-01; shortly afterward, DC-HD-01 recorded a network logon for maria.lopez originating from WS-BCARTER-01. The records do not explain this cross-account, cross-workstation activity. (T014-00089, T014-00090, T014-00092, T014-00112)

Separate review: proxy records show connections with GoogleDriveFS and DropboxUpdate user agents, while the inventory says Google Drive and Dropbox/file-sharing services are not approved. These records do not establish file transfer or a connection to the alerted PowerShell activity. (T014-00218, T014-00219, T014-00285, T014-00286)

Separate review: FILE-HD-01 recorded an SMB network logon as ANONYMOUS LOGON from WS-MLOPEZ-01 at 13:43:16. The records do not establish what resource was accessed or whether the activity succeeded beyond the logon. (T014-00213, T014-00217)
